video_title: Walker Kessler Wants Out of Utah | Lakers Collective

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ward
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler is unhappy with the Utah Jazz and seeking a move
quotes.excerpt: Walker Kessler does not see eye to eye with the Utah Jazz

text_blocks.speaker: Ryan Ward
text_blocks.text: A report came out last night from Sam Amick that Walker Kessler does not see eye to eye with the Utah Jazz and he is not pleased with the way things have gone so far. It is not necessarily a surprise because he is a restricted free agent, but the fact that it is being made public that Walker Kessler is not happy and is considering a future away from the Utah Jazz is certainly difficult to create when you are a restricted free agent.

text_blocks.speaker: Yovan
text_blocks.text: I would say there is some chance the door feels cracked open right now, depending on the type of offer the Lakers make, whether that is a financial offer or a potential sign and trade.

quotes.speaker: Yovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers should prioritize acquiring Walker Kessler over other potential targets
quotes.excerpt: I think Walker Kessler is already better than Jaxson Hayes and more proven
quotes.quote: If we are giving up a first-round pick for Jaxson Hayes, I think Walker Kessler is already better than Jaxson Hayes and more proven and ready for the moment. So, I would easily give up a first-round pick for Kessler in a potential sign and trade that would hard cap you at the first apron.

quotes.speaker: Yovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers have a narrow path to acquire Kessler while remaining under the first apron
quotes.excerpt: There is technically a way for LA to go above the cap, keep everybody, and also execute a sign and trade
quotes.quote: There is technically a way for LA to go above the cap, keep everybody, and also execute a sign and trade and stay under the first apron. That would depend on Austin Reaves's contract, which would really matter into this. LeBron James's contract, Rui Hachimura's contract, and you would probably have to use part of your non-taxpayer MLE on Marcus unless he is willing to just resign at that 6.3 cap hold. But there is a scenario here where if D'Angelo Russell opts out and you tell him we agreed to something with Walker Kessler, the second free agency starts, we are doing a sign and trade, you are not going to play, D'Angelo Russell opts out and goes elsewhere, and then you could maybe dump Jarred Vanderbilt as well. If you do those two moves, you can acquire Walker Kessler into your cap sheet, stay under the first apron, and now you have added Walker Kessler basically to last year's team in place of D'Angelo Russell.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ward
quotes.summary_phrase: John Hollinger predicts DeAndre Ayton will opt out of his contract
quotes.excerpt: John Hollinger predicted that DeAndre Ayton is going to opt out
quotes.quote: John Hollinger at The Athletic does a prediction column every year going into free agency that is pretty accurate, and he predicted that DeAndre Ayton is going to opt out. He thinks that DeAndre Ayton is going to get offers upwards of the non-taxpayer MLE, even if it is in a backup situation.

quotes.speaker: Yovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah holds significant leverage in any potential Walker Kessler trade
quotes.excerpt: Utah holds so much power in this situation
quotes.quote: In restricted free agency, Utah holds so much power in this situation and Kessler's injury history actually puts even more power into the hands of the Utah Jazz.
